Gets the help text that describes what a password must contain. It is shown in the UI wherever a user creates or changes a password. Anyone can call this.
Gets the free form UI configuration set for this agent server. Anyone can call this.
Fetches a document the UI needs at runtime, such as the agent schema or the UI text. The agent server checks for the latest version and serves it from an in-memory cache. Anyone can call this.

post.summary: Start connecting an integration to a user
post.description: Creates a request for a user to approve in the browser, so an integration can act as them without ever handling their password. Anyone can call this: an unapproved request grants nothing.
What the approval page shows before the user decides. It returns only what is already on their screen or where they started, and nothing about any user.

post.summary: Collect the token for an approved connect request
post.description: Called repeatedly by the integration until the user has approved, and then once more to receive the token. The secret is what authorizes it, and the request is used up once the token is handed over.
This is used to log out of the system from the UI.

post.summary: Create a draft for a new agent

post.summary: Create a draft for an existing agent
post.description: Creates a draft to make changes to an existing agent, and returns its draftid (the agent name). Succeeds whether the draft was created or already existed.

post.summary: Update a draft for a new agent
post.description: Updates a draft that is not yet a published agent, where the name and tag are still the developer's to choose. Only draftid is required: any field left out keeps its current value.

post.summary: Update a draft of an existing agent
post.description: Updates a draft taken from a published agent. The name and tag belong to the agent and cannot be changed here. Only draftid is required: any field left out keeps its current value.

post.summary: Merge a draft with its published agent
post.description: Reconciles a draft of an existing agent with the version of that agent published since the draft was created, and saves the result. The merged definition is produced for you and returned, so nothing about it is sent in. Use this when getDraft reports draftAgentHasChanged.

Writes an agent outline from a description of what it should do. The outline is returned, not saved, and a developer completes it: anything specific to your own systems, such as SQL or an API path, is left for you to fill in.
Get a draft agent.
This publishes the draft agent to the system. It returns success false with didMetaChange when the agent's title, run limits or prompts were changed after the draft was made and overwrite is off.
Deletes one or more draft agents. This has no effect on the system, as drafts exist purely in a developer's personal space.
Get all the drafts that have been created by this user.
Get all the agents in the system.
Gets an agent's definition and its descriptor.
Gets a list of past versions of an agent.

post.summary: Get a past version of an agent
post.description: Gets a past version of an agent. Only the versions from the last three months are maintained.
Changes how long a run of a published agent may take and how much LLM spend it may reach. Both are required: an agent is never unlimited. This does not make a new version of the agent.
Changes the title of one agent. The title is what users see when the agent is shown to them.
Changes the tag of one agent. The tag decides which searches can find the agent.
Deletes an agent from the system. This can be done only after removing the agent from the search index.
Publish an agent descriptor and index it for search. The call returns when indexing is done, usually in about 15 seconds. Do not retry a slow call: a retry starts a second indexing of the same agent.
Removes the agent from the search index so it can no longer be found by a search.
Gets the workspace audit log, newest first — for example, submissions of agents for indexing or removal and their outcomes. Can be narrowed by time range and entry type.
Answer a question on Search2o documentation.
Sends a message to Search2o support. The reply goes to the email address of the user who sent it.

Runs the draft against its validation query, with tracing on. Progress and traces can be streamed with stream=true. A draft must validate before it can be published.
Finds the agents that best match the search query.
Execute an agent. Agent responses can be streamed with stream=true.
Shows the current license key and, during a rotation, the old key and when it expires. Keys are shown by their last four characters only.

This call is used to periodically rotate the license key of the system. The old license will still stay active until the time specified here. The servers must be restarted within this duration, with the new license key.
This will cancel a pending license rotation, if the old/current license key has not expired. The new license key will be immediately invalid.

Rotates the account's encryption key. New data is encrypted with the new key, while data encrypted with earlier keys stays readable. Agent servers keep using the previous key until they are restarted. The key can be rotated at most once every 90 days.
Adds a list of users to the system with the role provided.
This call fetches all the users in the system.
This call fetches a single user in the system.
Deletes users from the system. Once deleted, a user cannot be recovered. Users with a role of owner can be deleted only by another owner.

Modifies a user's role. Users can run searches and execute agents. Developers can draft and publish agents and descriptors. They can also change the environment configuration. Lists the service accounts, ordered by name. A service account is a program rather than a person, so it is listed here rather than with the users.

Creates a service account and answers its key. The key is returned once and is stored nowhere, so keep it; if it is lost, rotate the key to get another. A service account may hold any role except owner.
Issues a new key for a service account. The previous key stops working immediately. The new key is returned once and is stored nowhere.
Changes what a service account may do. Any role except owner. A service account's role cannot be changed with updateRole, which is for people.
Deletes a service account. Its key stops working immediately and the account cannot be recovered. A service account cannot be deleted with deleteUsers, which is for people.
This call can be made to stop any changes to agents or descriptors in the system. No new agents can be published either. Developers can still create draft agents and run them.
Unfreezes the system.

Gets one of the configurations. See the documentation for more details.
Gets one of the configurations. See the documentation for more details.
Updates part of the configuration. See the documentation for more details.

post.summary: Add or update a collection config object
post.description: Add or update one of the objects in a collection configuration. See the documentation for more details.

This call is made when the user updates the password from the profile page in the UI.
This call is made when the user updates their name or UI preferences.

Sets the title shown for a conversation in the user's list. By default a conversation is titled with its first query.
Pins a conversation so it is kept and listed separately, or unpins it. There is a limit on how many conversations one user may pin.
Deletes one of the user's own conversations, along with everything the agent saved in it. This cannot be undone.

What integrations can act as this user, when each was created and when it was last used, so that any of them can be revoked.
Stops that token working immediately. Nothing else is affected: not the user's browser session and not their other integrations.
Approving mints a token for this user, limited to what an end user may do, and hands it to the integration that asked. The token is never returned to the browser.

Report which agents failed, how often, and with which result codes
Report LLM cost stats for each agent
